properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued October 18 at 2:59PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8
inches possible.

* WHERE...Fairbanks North Star Borough and Nenana.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lighter snow is expected Monday with some
mixed precipitation possible. Heavier snow is possible Tuesday.
There is high uncertainty in the exact snow amounts and the
placement of the heavier snow. This detail will be crucial in
determining which spots get 6"+ and 3" or less. As of right now, we
are leaning towards the heaviest snow being towards Eielson with
lighter snow in Fairbanks and especially west of Fairbanks. A 30
mile change east or west will result in drastic differences. We
will continue to update as details become clearer.
properties.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 18 to 36
inches expected above 2500 feet with higher amounts above pass
level and 12 to 24 inches expected below 2500 feet. Winds could
gust as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Alaska Range.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Monday to 4 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Areas of
blowing snow could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Following strong southerly winds north of
Trims Camp on Monday, heavy snow is expected to build in Monday
into Tuesday and Wednesday as winds shift to being out of the
north.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, water and warm
clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 5 and
10 inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be a narrow snow gradient. The
highest potential for heavy snow lies southeast of Fort Yukon. West
and north of there, the likelihood for heavier snow drops quickly.
Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting 1 to 3
inches or less from this.

vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit 511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1
